A04D5A.name: Religie, zingeving en levensbeschouwing
A04D5A.content: Deze cursus gaat niet zozeer over de vraag welke ruimte zingeving, levensbeschouwing en religie krijgen in de samenleving en in mijn leven, maar eerder welke ruimte zingeving, levensbeschouwing en religie geven. The course provides theoretical tools for critically examining these topics through the lens of "mystagogische ruimte" (mystical spaces), using case studies primarily from Christian contexts (churches, chapels, cathedrals). Four dimensions are explored: synaesthetic, kerygmatic, liturgical, and eschatological. Students work in teams to design a mystical space addressing contemporary societal needs using methods from Jozef Cardijn and liberation theology.
A04D5A.learningOutcomes: Students will be able to: clarify religion's role in culture and society; analyze worldviews in media, healthcare, economics, technology, and education; demonstrate the distinctiveness of Christian faith traditions; apply theological theories to current social issues; engage critically with religious themes in their field; develop personal, substantiated perspectives on worldview questions; recognize religion's value in their own lives; integrate these dimensions into professional identity development; and critically reflect on religion's role today.
A04D5A.prerequisites: Dit college vergt geen specifieke voorkennis. Students need not be religious but should be willing to reflecteren over fundamentele ethische en zingevingsvragen vanuit verschillende levensbeschouwelijke invalshoeken.
A04D5A.evaluation: Continuous evaluation without exam period. Students complete 20% practical exercises, present projects midterm (20% presentation, 20% peer feedback), and present final designs with thematic modules (40%). All team members must participate actively in both presentations.

A08C4A.name: Religie, zingeving en levensbeschouwing
A08C4A.content: Vanuit moderne menswetenschappelijke inzichten en vanuit het eigentijdse theologische denken worden enkele thema's uit de actuele zingevingsproblematiek behandeld. The course addresses: purpose of religions, Christian faith core, positioning within world religions, Christianity-culture relations, classical theological themes throughout centuries, faith and personal happiness, Christian future expectations versus humanistic objections, faith-science debate, ethical distinctiveness, and engineering ethics relevance.
A08C4A.learningOutcomes: Eight learning outcomes focus on: clarifying religion's role in culture, analyzing worldviews in societal phenomena, demonstrating faith traditions' distinctiveness, applying theological theories to contemporary issues, addressing religious themes in one's field, developing personal grounded perspectives, recognizing life meaning value, and integrating worldview dimensions into professional identity.
A08C4A.prerequisites: Dit college vergt geen specifieke voorkennis. However, general knowledge of philosophy, ethics, Western culture and history is assumed. Students need openness to critical-scientific reflection on fundamental ethical questions from various worldview perspectives.
A08C4A.evaluation: First exam: multiple choice. Ongeveer 20 procent van de vragen peilt naar kennis; 80 procent zijn denkvragen. Retakes consist of three open-ended questions.

D0M36A.name: Environmental Economics
D0M36A.content: Foundational environmental and resource economics, Environmental valuations, Cost and benefit analysis and discounting, Integrated Assessment Models for Climate Change, Government Responses to Pollution problems, International Environmental Agreements.
D0M36A.learningOutcomes: Students should demonstrate an understanding of key approaches and methods in environmental and resource economics, and demonstrate an ability to analyse and apply taught models and techniques in environmental economics, pollution and transportation problems.
D0M36A.prerequisites: Basic knowledge of micro-economics (demand, supply, market equilibrium, imperfect competition) and quantitative techniques (algebraic treatment of micro-economics) is essential. No prior transportation science knowledge required.
D0M36A.evaluation: Closed-book written exam with essay based and conceptual/model-based questions.

D0S18A.name: Technology Entrepreneurship and New Business Development
D0S18A.content: The course combines theoretical foundations with practical application. Students explore entrepreneurial decision-making through lectures covering idea generation, feasibility studies, business plan development, industry and market analysis, marketing strategy, team formation, operations, product development, and financial planning. The practical component requires groups to develop comprehensive operational business plans for technology-intensive ventures.
D0S18A.learningOutcomes: Upon completion, students can explain and illustrate the unique qualities of the entrepreneurial decision-making process and develop sophisticated business plans. They learn to evaluate product ideas, assess business model feasibility in high-tech sectors, and conduct primary research. The course emphasizes responsible entrepreneurship, requiring students to critically assess the risks and challenges associated with business growth.
D0S18A.prerequisites: This course does not assume that you have taken prior classes on entrepreneurship or business administration. However, basic organizational knowledge helps, though entrepreneurial ventures differ substantially from generic business management.
D0S18A.evaluation: Grading comprises three components: 30% written multiple-choice exam, 50% final business plan, and 20% presentations. Peer evaluation may adjust business plan grades by up to 20%. Missing deadlines or non-participation results in "NA" grades.
D0S18A.teachingMethods: Students interactively acquire in-depth and advanced insights through a course combining traditional lectures with a demanding field project.

G0B01A.name: Intellectual Property Management
G0B01A.content: The lectures are divided into theoretical modules and guest lectures. Theoretical modules cover basic rules of patent law, copyright, and trademark law in accessible language with practical examples. Guest speakers from academia, industry, and practice discuss broader economic frameworks and protection strategies companies employ during research, development, and product launch stages, emphasizing IP management in practice.
G0B01A.learningOutcomes: Upon completion, students can: understand knowledge and technology protection importance; comprehend intellectual property basics including patents, copyrights, trademarks, and designs; understand how companies strategically use IP systems; use domain-specific terminology; grasp protection versus secrecy trade-offs and associated strategies; answer practical IP protection and management questions; and conduct initial analyses of protection possibilities for new creations.
G0B01A.prerequisites: Het college gaat ervan uit dat de studenten geen voorkennis inzake recht in het algemeen of intellectuele rechten in het bijzonder bezitten. (The course assumes students possess no prior knowledge of law generally or intellectual property specifically.)
G0B01A.evaluation: Individual written exam (2 hours) with two possible timing options. The exam comprises three equally-weighted sections; at least two use the provided question list. The third may include an open essay requiring structured, comprehensible, and substantively correct advice on concrete IP protection and policy issues.

H00C0A.name: Materials Selection
H00C0A.content: Overview on material classes: Metallic materials, Polymers, Ceramics, Composites. Review on material properties and concomitant measurement techniques. Materials properties and their visual interpretation using material selection charts. Material Selection Methodology using the Grantadesign CES Edupack software (Ashby principle). Review of Material Processing Techniques. Process selection methodology. Case studies focussing on Material and Process Selection. Eco-Audit tool to perform Life Cycle Impact Analysis.
H00C0A.learningOutcomes: The aims of the course are twofold: on the one hand provide the students with a broad overview of all classes of materials and their salient properties. On the other hand to provide a general method of selection of materials in thermo-mechanical design.
H00C0A.prerequisites: General physics and chemistry; introductory courses in materials science covering elementary concepts on microstructure and phase diagrams and on material properties.
H00C0A.evaluation: The students are evaluated based on an assignment, targeting a materials and process selection for a component at choice. They will hand in a 20 page written report and will come and orally defend their report during an oral exam, which will last approximately 30 minutes.

H00K1A.name: Engineering Economy
H00K1A.content: Exercises and cases are solved and discussed. Case studies are exercises placed in a realistic business context; they call for more analysis and insight than classic exercises.
H00K1A.learningOutcomes: The student has a broad view on economical (decision oriented) problems engineers will encounter in their professional career. The student obtains insights in methods such as PW, FW and AW, C/B calculations, replacement decision making and cost estimation.
H00K1A.prerequisites: Bachelor engineering or other bachelor in science & technology.
H00K1A.evaluation: Written exam during the examination period with multiple choice and open questions. Permitted materials include list of formulas and calculator.

H00M4A.name: Maintenance Management
H00M4A.content: The course addresses managerial issues in asset/maintenance management for organizations both in industry (production plants) and service industry (hospitals, distribution centra, ...). Topics included are: organization of the maintenance department, personnel management, auditing and performance reporting, maintenance concept decisions.
H00M4A.learningOutcomes: The student knows the theoretical foundations for analyzing and optimizing maintenance situations. The student obtains insight in the practical issues of maintenance and asset management, both in industry and service organizations.
H00M4A.prerequisites: Bachelor of engineering or other bachelor science & technology.
H00M4A.evaluation: Partial or continuous assessment with (final) exam during the examination period. Assessment method: Oral, Paper/Project. Type of questions: Open questions. Permitted materials: Calculator.
H00M4A.teachingMethods: Classes: partly ex cathedra, mainly interactive. Theory, exercises and cases (guided independent study).

H00N6A.name: Total Quality Management
H00N6A.content: The course covers foundational TQM concepts and historical context, organizational implementation in industrial and service environments, management roles, worker behavior, quality systems per ISO 9000, and quantitative techniques including statistical process control, Pareto analysis, and Ishikawa diagrams.
H00N6A.learningOutcomes: Introduction to Total Quality Management (TQM): philosophy and concepts (part I), tools and techniques (part II).
H00N6A.evaluation: Written examination during the examination period featuring multiple-choice and open-ended questions. A formularium will be provided. For the multiple choice questions a guess correction is used.

H00O3A.name: Ecodesign and Life Cycle Engineering
H00O3A.content: Introduction: course info, positioning, overview of the most important environmental effects. Life cycle analysis (LCA). DfE techniques: Design guidelines, LIDS wheel, MET matrix, Material choice techniques, EPIndicators, DfE Toolboxes, DfR/DfD techniques, Fast LCA methods, Parametric LCA, Life Cycle Costing, Retraction logistics, Industrial ecosystems, Legislation and norms, Software-support: workshop Eco Indicator, Idemat, Case Studies, Final presentations by the students.
H00O3A.learningOutcomes: The course aims to develop awareness regarding how design choices impact products throughout their lifecycle. It presents analytical methods for evaluating products and optimizing designs while emphasizing environmental consequences. The instruction focuses on developing engineers who understand their ecological influence and can contribute to sustainable resource management, while also balancing business economics and technical feasibility.
H00O3A.prerequisites: The student has a solid scientific background, preferably engineering.
H00O3A.evaluation: A final assignment per two students results in a report that is presented during the exam period followed by a question session.

H01Z4A.name: Production Systems: Machine Tools, Flexible Computer Integrated Production
H01Z4A.content: Concepts for production machines and systems; Construction of machine tools; Tool spindles; Clamping, slides, guides, drives, positioning systems; Controllers (PLC, NC programming); Flexible production systems; Thermal stability; Dynamic behavior; Quality control.
H01Z4A.learningOutcomes: Students learn machine tool and flexible manufacturing system structures, analyze production systems, explain component functions, design machines from specifications, understand automation methods, learn thermal/dynamic behavior improvements, and understand purchase procedures including accuracy measurement.
H01Z4A.prerequisites: Basic knowledge of machine construction (machine elements), production techniques and materials. Basic knowledge CAD.
H01Z4A.evaluation: Part 'Production Machines and Systems': Oral exam. Part 'Computer Integrated Production': Written exam. Both closed book. Lab attendance mandatory; unjustified absence results in 0/20 for entire course.
H01Z4A.teachingMethods: Classical lectures using PowerPoint presentations with blackboard notes; Online lectures; Practical lab sessions in groups of 4 using CAD/CAM system ESPRIT; Independent student work.

H02A4A.name: Robotics
H02A4A.content: Introduction to software development for robots, robot kinematics and dynamics, robot motion control and sensor-guided control, free-space and in-contact tasks, trajectory optimization, dealing with uncertainty / estimation in robotics, classical motion planning and learning methods for motion planning, learning from demonstration; plus computer exercises and interactive lab visits.
H02A4A.learningOutcomes: Students should be able to analyse, develop, and use kinematic and dynamic models of robot systems, design motion and sensor-guided control strategies, and identify what aspects lend themselves to AI solutions in robotics applications.
H02A4A.prerequisites: Background in programming, engineering mechanics, linear algebra and basic differential and integral calculus. Master-level background expected.
H02A4A.evaluation: Oral defence covering both the homework assignment and the research project. The homework assignment counts for 25% of the grade, the research project for 75%.
H02A4A.lecturer: Aertbeliën Erwin, Decré Wilm (Coordinator), Detry Renaud

H02D2A.name: Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence
H02D2A.content: Graphical-model approaches to reasoning under uncertainty, including Bayesian networks, Markov networks (Markov random fields), factor graphs, and hidden Markov models; modelling, inference and learning within these formalisms; applications, and integration of uncertainty reasoning with logic-based reasoning and learning.
H02D2A.learningOutcomes: Understand and appreciate the role and need for uncertainty in AI systems; know, understand and apply the graphical-model approach to uncertainty, including the underlying algorithms; understand how techniques for reasoning about uncertainty can be integrated with logic for reasoning and learning.
H02D2A.prerequisites: Familiarity with basic concepts of discrete probability and mathematics. Knowledge of calculus is useful but not required.
H02D2A.evaluation: Type: Partial or continuous assessment with (final) exam during the examination period. Assessment method: Report, Written. Type of questions: Open questions. Permitted materials: List of formulas, Calculator. The exam can be retaken; the assignments cannot.
H02D2A.teachingMethods: Lecture combined with exercises/practical sessions and project work.
H02D2A.lecturer: De Raedt Luc (De Laet Tinne as co-lecturer)

H02V8A.name: Design and Analysis of Experimentation
H02V8A.content: Data summary, Data visualization, Statistical hypothesis testing, Analysis of variance (ANOVA), Design of experiments, Full and fractional factorial analysis, Regression, Response surface method
H02V8A.learningOutcomes: Students will be able to describe and analyze experimental datasets and design campaigns minimizing workload. They understand features and limitations of statistical techniques, can choose suitable methods for drawing statistically significant conclusions, and can use statistical software while judging validity based on calculations.
H02V8A.prerequisites: Mathematical background (linear algebra, analysis); Basic programming knowledge (Python or MATLAB)
H02V8A.evaluation: Two-part evaluation: project report (8/20) and written exam (12/20). Students may choose to repeat the project; the exam must be repeated.
H02V8A.teachingMethods: Flipped classroom format with knowledge clips provided before contact hours. Contact hours emphasize exercises with concepts demonstrated on paper examples and software tools for larger datasets. Students conduct independent projects applying learned techniques.

H03U4A.name: Biomaterials
H03U4A.content: The first part of the course will give an overview of the host environment and define the requirements for the biomaterials to be used in it. In the next part, the specific material classes (metals, ceramics, polymers and their composites) are discussed in more detail, with special attention to specific examples of biomaterials in every material class. The course concludes with a series of seminars given by medical specialists who will focus on biomaterials used in specific clinical applications, such as reconstructive surgery, cardiovascular surgery, orthopedic surgery, traumatology, abdominal surgery and dental applications.
H03U4A.learningOutcomes: Students can explain different properties of non-viable biomaterials used for biomedical devices. Specifically, students evaluate host environments and device functions; understand physical, chemical, and mechanical properties; explain how manufacturing processes govern material properties; and propose new materials for applications.
H03U4A.evaluation: Type: Exam during the examination period. Assessment method: Written. Permitted materials: None

H03V7B.name: Data Mining and Neural Networks
H03V7B.content: Overview of main classical and advanced modern techniques on data mining and neural networks. Covers multilayer perceptrons, radial basis function networks, learning algorithms, optimization methods, generalization, feedforward and recurrent networks, pruning, variance reduction, regularization theory, classification, function estimation, preprocessing, feature selection, dimensionality reduction, Bayesian inference, deep learning, statistical learning theory, support vector machines, cluster algorithms, vector-quantization, self-organizing maps, principal component analysis, autoencoders, convolutional neural networks, generative models, transformers.
H03V7B.evaluation: Exam during the examination period. Assessment method: Oral, Written. Type of questions: Open questions. Permitted materials: Course material

H03Y1A.name: Theory of Elasticity and Plasticity
H03Y1A.content: The course is divided into two main parts: Part I covers elasticity topics including mathematical concepts, stress, kinematics and deformations, conservation laws, constitutive equations, 2D elasticity formulation, virtual work, potential energy, and shells. Part II addresses plasticity in one-dimensional stress states, yield criteria in multi-dimensional stress states, and deformations in the plastic regime.
H03Y1A.learningOutcomes: The student knows the concepts and quantities from solid mechanics and understands the relations between them. The student can write the full set of equations for an elastic and an elasto-plastic analysis of a body with an arbitrary shape in two- or three-dimensional space.
H03Y1A.prerequisites: Basic knowledge of strength of materials
H03Y1A.evaluation: Oral, Written exam during the examination period. Each student receives three questions: one theory question requiring independent deduction, and two exercises—one from elasticity and one from plasticity. Two questions are prepared in writing before oral discussion; the third is written only.
H03Y1A.lecturer: Degrande Geert and Vandepitte Dirk (Coordinator: Vandepitte Dirk)

H04B5B.name: Nuclear Energy: Basic Aspects
H04B5B.content: Topics include general introduction, nuclear energy's future, physical concepts for nuclear reactions, radiation interactions, nuclear fission, reactor types, fuel cycle, reactor control, thermal hydraulics, safety, and radioactive waste management.
H04B5B.learningOutcomes: Providing the students with a proper understanding of and thorough insight into all important aspects of nuclear electricity production.
H04B5B.prerequisites: The students need a thorough background in basic physics and thermodynamics. Knowledge of a course Technical Thermodynamics or Energy Conversion Machines and Systems is a useful extra source of knowledge.
H04B5B.evaluation: The exam consists of an oral examination but with written preparation. Students receive 20 minutes preparation time for two general questions (open book), followed by a 20-minute oral exam.

H04B5C.name: Nuclear Energy: Deepening Insights
H04B5C.content: Covers reactor theory, neutron behavior, kinetic and dynamic behavior of nuclear reactors, thermal hydraulics, economic aspects, nuclear energy's role in future electricity generation, and nuclear fuel resources.
H04B5C.learningOutcomes: To provide the students with a deeper understanding of the physical and technical basic principles of radioactivity, nuclear reactors and nuclear electricity generation.
H04B5C.prerequisites: The students must have had a first course on Nuclear Engineering and must take or have completed Nuclear Energy: Basic Aspects (H04B5B).
H04B5C.evaluation: Oral exam during the examination period with Multiple choice, Open questions, Closed questions permitted with access to course materials, calculator, and reference works.

H04C4A.name: Energy Economics
H04C4A.content: 1. Introduction to environmental and resource economics 2. Economics of sustainability, climate change and international energy policy 3. Characteristics and modelling of primary energy markets (oil, natural gas, coal) 4. Economic aspects of electricity markets with and without renewable energy
H04C4A.learningOutcomes: Understand and assess events on global energy markets; Make, or contribute to, business and policy decisions related to energy; Work as an engineer in multidisciplinary teams that involve economists
H04C4A.prerequisites: Knowledge of basic microeconomics (market balance, supply and demand curves, perfect competition and monopoly, discounted cash flow analysis) - Knowledge of calculus and mathematical optimisation
H04C4A.evaluation: Open-book, written exam, in which students are requested to solve novel economic problems/questions related to the course material

H04O1A.name: Aerodynamics
H04O1A.content: The course covers subsonic incompressible flows in vehicle and thermotechnology applications, transient flows, aerodynamic forces and centers, basic equations, vorticity and circulation, flow around profiles and wings, compressible and supersonic theory, viscous flows, and turbulence phenomena.
H04O1A.learningOutcomes: The aim of the course is to provide physical insight into the fundamental principles of subsonic and supersonic aerodynamics.
H04O1A.prerequisites: For this course, good knowledge of fluid mechanics and thermodynamics is required.
H04O1A.evaluation: Written exam during the examination period consisting of overview questions on theory and exercises. Permitted materials include a formula list and calculator.
H04O1A.teachingMethods: Lectures (34 hours) and practical exercises (9 hours), totaling 52 hours of instruction.
H04O1A.lecturer: Baelmans Tine (Coordinator), Dekeyser Wouter, and Meyers Johan

H04O1B.name: Aerodynamics
H04O1B.content: Introduction: properties of air, aerodynamic forces, typical variable ranges, influence of Re and Ma, pressure centre and aerodynamic centre. Basic equations: classification of flows, integral formulations to determine drag coefficients, differential formulations: use of tensor notation and curve-linear coordinates. Vorticity and circulation: evolution of thermodynamic variables through streamlines, transport of vorticity and circulation, origin of vorticity and circulation: the starting vortex. Subsonic incompressible flows around profiles: rotation-free flow, Kutta condition, influence of angle of attack, curvation and thickness, functioning of flaps, Joukowski's theorem, the vortex panel method. Subsonic incompressible flows around wings: downwash, tip vortices, elliptical wings, tapered wings and delta wings. Subsonic incompressible flows: applications in aviation: polar diagramme of an aeroplane, flight criteria, manoeuvres. Compressible flows: perturbation theory, Prandtl-Glauert's rule. Supersonic theory: Prandtl-Meyer expansion, normal shocks, oblique shocks, visualization, boundary layer interactions, the area rule. Viscous flows: energy dissipation, boundary layers, hypersonic comparisons. Turbulence: instability of a flow with rotation, primary and secondary instabilities, transition, statistic approach in turbulence
H04O1B.prerequisites: For this course, good knowledge of fluid mechanics and thermodynamics is required.
H04O1B.evaluation: The exam consists of an overview question on the theory (oral examination) and a number of exercises (written).

H04O7A.name: Bedrijfsstage: Werktuigkunde / Industrial Internship: Mechanical Engineering
H04O7A.content: De bedrijfservaring omvat een werkverblijf met een minimale duur van 4 weken in een bedrijf gedurende de maanden juli of augustus, tijdens de welke de student activiteiten zal uitoefenen.
H04O7A.learningOutcomes: De student kan na de korte bedrijfservaring een afdeling van een bedrijf situeren binnen het groter geheel van het bedrijf, het bedrijf binnen zijn sector en in het geheel van het industrieel weefsel.
H04O7A.prerequisites: Voorkennis: afwerken van een Bachelor Ingenieurswetenschappen: werktuigkunde.
H04O7A.evaluation: De evaluatie gebeurt aan de hand van een schriftelijke en mondelinge rapportering, bestaande uit een schriftelijk verslag (15-20 pagina's) opgedeeld in drie delen en een mondelinge presentatie (15 minuten) gevolgd door vragen.

H04P5A.name: Embedded Control Systems
H04P5A.content: The course covers embedded control systems with emphasis on smart moving machines (robots, cars, trucks, etc.), innovation project engineering roles, systems-level thinking, innovative design methodology, and design automation standards and tools.
H04P5A.learningOutcomes: This course introduces students to the software and hardware aspects of embedded and realtime computer-controlled machine tools, robots, vehicles and instruments, in the specific context of mechatronic systems-of-systems.
H04P5A.prerequisites: SIMULTANEOUS(H04X3B) OR SIMULTANEOUS(H00S4A) OR SIMULTANEOUS(H00S3A) OR SIMULTANEOUS(H04X3A) - students must take one of these control theory courses simultaneously. Required prior knowledge: Bachelor level of mechanical dynamical systems. Passive knowledge of a higher programming language, and of computer infrastructure.
H04P5A.evaluation: Continuous assessment without exam during the examination period, using process evaluation, skills tests, and take-home assignments with open questions. Homeworks, autonomous exploration assignments, and interactive project sessions with feedback.

H04P9A.name: Integrated Project
H04P9A.content: This course consists of one or more cross-curricular activities, with sufficient depth with respect to the core mechanical courses, a partial option specific interpretation is also included.
H04P9A.learningOutcomes: The objective of this course is to acquire the following competencies with limited guidance: integration of the contents of the courses from the core training mechanics and some cluster-specific courses; application of design methodologies in practical assignments; ability to work in group and to give oral and written reports on technical and scientific work.
H04P9A.prerequisites: SIMULTANEOUS(H04S6A) AND SIMULTANEOUS(H04U3A) AND (SIMULTANEOUS(H04X3A) OR SIMULTANEOUS(H04X3B)) AND SIMULTANEOUS(H04X7A) AND (SIMULTANEOUS(H0H51A) OR SIMULTANEOUS(H03Y1A)) OR SIMULTANEOUS(H00R7A) OR (SIMULTANEOUS(H00S3A) OR SIMULTANEOUS(H00S4A)) OR SIMULTANEOUS(H07S3A) OR SIMULTANEOUS(H00R8A) OR SIMULTANEOUS(H00S2A)
H04P9A.evaluation: Presentation, Report based on technical quality of the development and/or the scientific merit of the analysis. The quality of both the oral and the written part of reporting are taken into account.
H04P9A.teachingMethods: The sessions include a limited number of general seminars on CAD/CAE and a major project conducted over the entire semester with intermediate and final presentations.
H04P9A.lecturer: Bruyninckx Herman, Castagne Sylvie, Gorissen Benjamin, Gryllias Konstantinos, Helsen Lieve, Naets Frank, Swevers Jan, Vandepitte Dirk, Vetrano Maria Rosaria, Vrancken Bey

H04Q1B.name: Advanced Thermodynamics and Plasma Physics
H04Q1B.content: Part I: Kinetic theory and statistical thermodynamics applied to fluid mechanics, covering Fluid Equations, Distribution Functions, Collisional Processes, Chapman-Enskog Method, and Grad's equations. Part II: Application of kinetic theory and statistical thermodynamics to plasmas, addressing charged particles, plasma behavior in fields, transport models, MHD equations, and fusion applications.
H04Q1B.learningOutcomes: To provide the students with in-depth insight of kinetic theory and statistical thermodynamics.
H04Q1B.prerequisites: The course is open to students with a thorough knowledge of thermal engineering, such as technical thermodynamics, heat transfer, and fluid mechanics.
H04Q1B.evaluation: Oral examination with open and closed questions. Students receive 30 minutes for open-book preparation followed by 30 minutes of oral examination for each part (Part I and Part II), testing overall insight into the material.

H04Q4A.name: Advanced Techniques for Vibro-acoustic Measurement and Analysis
H04Q4A.content: Lectures are given on the following topics: Acoustic Modal Analysis, Measurement of acoustic quantities (sound power, acoustic intensity, acoustic impedance), Digital signal processing for acoustic analysis, Time-frequency analysis (RPM and order tracking, SFFT, wavelet analysis), Transfer path analysis, panel contribution analysis, Subjective noise evaluation, Active Noise and Vibration Control, Workshop: Vibro acoustic measurements at LMS International.
H04Q4A.learningOutcomes: The student acquires knowledge on recent vibro-acoustic measurement and analysis techniques, with special attention for automotive NVH problems (Noise and Vibration Harshness). The student is capable of selecting the optimal technique for a given problem and of motivating his choice, he has a clear view on the weaknesses and strengths of the different techniques and is capable of critically interpreting the results. He is aware of the relevant scientific publications in this field and is capable of reviewing a related scientific paper.
H04Q4A.prerequisites: Machine design, Mechanical Vibrations, Measurement systems, Signal processing, control theory.
H04Q4A.evaluation: Open book exam (including calculator) and discussion on the exam paper (15 min). Discussion of a scientific paper (15 min).
H04Q4A.teachingMethods: Lectures, literature search, discussion forum, workshop at LMS International.
H04Q4A.lecturer: Gryllias Konstantinos and Van Der Auweraer Herman

H04Q7A.name: Advanced Model Based Control
H04Q7A.content: 1. Introduction to system identification, differences between time and frequency domain identification, properties of parameter estimation methods, relation between different approaches. 2. Frequency identification of linear time invariant systems: design of excitation signals for frequency response function measurement, estimation of frequency response functions (FRFs), deterministic and stochastic frequency domain identification methods (parametric models), model validation techniques, estimation of the influence of nonlinear distortions on accuracy of FRF measurements. 3. Advanced control design: differences between collocated and non-collocated control, basics of model-inversion based feedforward control design, robust loopshaping feedback control design, mixed-sensitivity H-infinity control design, introduction to iterative learning control design.
H04Q7A.learningOutcomes: The student is able to perform frequency domain identification experiments and to critically evaluate the obtained results, and this using available Matlab-code. The student is able to design advanced feedback and feedforward controllers based on performance and robustness specifications in time and/or frequency domain, estimates of system model uncertainty, and this using available Matlab-code. The student is able to apply these methods on a mechatronic single-input motion system. The student is able to interpret, evaluate and present the obtained results, and motivate the choices made during the design.
H04Q7A.prerequisites: Linear systems theory and the fundamentals of linear control theory form the starting point of the course contents. Thus, a thorough knowledge of and insight in these matters are an important prerequisite for students who wish to add this course to their program. Formal prerequisites: FLEXIBLE (H00S3A) OR FLEXIBLE (H00S4A) OR FLEXIBLE (H04X3A) OR FLEXIBLE (H04X3B).
H04Q7A.evaluation: The students present the results of their individual assignment and of their group research project. During these presentations, the students are questioned about the results. Important elements of the evaluation are: knowledge of the course material, commitment of the students during the project implementation, critical analysis of results, critical attitude of the student, quality of presentation, response of the students during discussion. The individual assignment and project assignment respectively account for 25% and 75% of the total score.

H04Q9A.name: Industriële stage: Werktuigkunde / Industrial Internship: Mechanical Engineering
H04Q9A.content: De stage omvat een werkverblijf met een minimale duur van 6 weken in een bedrijf gedurende de maanden juli of augustus, tijdens de welke de opdracht beschreven in een bij voorbaat duidelijk uitgewerkt stageplan wordt uitgevoerd.
H04Q9A.learningOutcomes: De student kan na de stage een afdeling van een bedrijf situeren binnen het groter geheel van het bedrijf, het bedrijf binnen zijn sector en in het geheel van het industrieel weefsel.
H04Q9A.prerequisites: Voorkennis: afwerken van een Bachelor Ingenieurswetenschappen: werktuigkunde.
H04Q9A.evaluation: De evaluatie gebeurt aan de hand van een schriftelijke en mondelinge stagerapportering in overeenstemming met volgende richtlijnen.

H04S6A.name: Mechanical Drive Systems
H04S6A.learningOutcomes: Introducing the student into the most commonly used mechanical drive systems: combustion motors, pneumatic and hydraulic drives. The student should be able to describe the concepts and thinking patterns around mechanical drives (reproduction).
H04S6A.prerequisites: Classical thermodynamics, heat transfer, theory of flows, kinematics and dynamics of mechanisms, principles of machine construction. Elementary knowledge of electricity, dynamics, vibrations, systems theory, machine elements and control technology is required.
H04S6A.evaluation: The examination is based on the lectures as well as on the exercises. The student gets 4 questions: Question 1 on combustion engines, Question 2 on combustion engines, Question 3 on pneumatics, Question 4 on hydraulics.
H04S6A.teachingMethods: Teaching course in a large auditorium. Slides with video animations. Guided exercise in a group of about 20 students. During these exercises Matlab is used as an engineering tool.
H04S6A.lecturer: Reynaerts Dominiek (Coordinator) and Vetrano Maria Rosaria

H04U1C.name: Optimization of Mechatronic Systems
H04U1C.content: Lecture content covers: Introduction with motivating examples and mathematical modeling; algorithms for continuous optimization without constraints (line search, gradient-based, Newton methods); algorithms with constraints (KKT conditions, simplex, interior point methods, convex optimization); global optimization methods (deterministic and stochastic); and software discussion. Practical content includes: guided exercise sessions on appropriate formulations of problems as (convex) optimization problems; independent project work: formulate and solve a mechatronic optimization problem.
H04U1C.learningOutcomes: The student will be able to formulate optimization problems from engineering contexts, classify problems by type, select appropriate strategies, formulate optimality conditions, understand various algorithms, use optimization software, and independently solve practical mechatronic optimization problems.
H04U1C.prerequisites: Basic knowledge of analysis, numerical mathematics, and numerical linear algebra, plus basic knowledge of systems and control, kinematics and dynamics of machinery, mechanical vibrations and electrical machines.
H04U1C.evaluation: Written exam for the lecture; oral exam based on independent project work for exercises/lab sessions. Grade calculated as weighted sum using ECTS credits.
H04U1C.lecturer: Patrinos Panos (Lecture); Decré Wilm (Exercises and Laboratory Sessions, Coordinator)

H04U3A.name: Numerical Modelling in Mechanical Engineering
H04U3A.content: Spatial discretization and interpolation, discrete implementation of boundary conditions, time integration schemes, linearization of non-linear governing systems, introduction to finite-volume discretization for Navier-Stokes equations, mathematical characterization of PDEs, Taylor series development for accuracy determination, Von Neuman stability analyses.
H04U3A.learningOutcomes: Students are able to explain modern methods for numerical simulation of phenomena and systems in mechanical engineering. For simple problems, students elaborate numerical discretization methods into computational code, verify and validate implementation, use modern commercial software, argument choices of techniques, and perform critical assessment of simulation results based on mathematical relationships for numerical method analysis.
H04U3A.prerequisites: Fundamental knowledge of physical phenomena in mechanics: heat transfer, fluid mechanics, structural mechanics. Basic mathematical techniques: solution of normal and partial differential equations, numeral integration, solution of systems of algebraic equations, eigenvalue problems.
H04U3A.evaluation: Exam during the examination period. Assessment method: Written. Type of questions: Open questions. Permitted materials: Course material.

H04U8A.name: Numerical Techniques in Fluid Dynamics
H04U8A.content: Formuleren en discretiseren van onsamendrukbare Navier-Stokes (NS) vergelijkingen met behulp van eindige volume techniek. Oplossen van grote niet-lineaire discrete stelsels volgend uit de discretisatie van de NS vergelijkingen: Newtongebaseerde methodes, time marching (expliciet versus impliciet), keuze linearisatie, ontkoppeling van de vergelijkingen. Gebruik van 'pressure-correction' technieken voor het ontkoppelen van de druk bij linearisatie. Inleiding tot het oplossen van grote lineaire stelsels en gevolgen voor keuzes met betrekking tot linearisatie en ontkoppeling.
H04U8A.learningOutcomes: Based on specialised literature, handbooks and own knowledge, the student is able to select an appropriate numerical scheme for simulation problems in fluid mechanics, which appear in application areas related to automobile industry, aerospace, energy conversion technology, air conditioning, etc. The student is capable of implementing these techniques in their most simple version, and is able to verify and validate them.
H04U8A.prerequisites: Basic knowledge of numerical methods, and in particular finite-difference, and finite-volume techniques. Additionally, students must simultaneously take one of: H04U3A, H00R8A, H9X34A, or H00S9A.
H04U8A.evaluation: The evaluation is based on three aspects: the presentation of the selected literature subject to peer students (during the term), 30% of the points; the implementation of a NS code (70% of the points), based on the report on the verification and validation, and the submitted code.

H04V5A.name: Deterministic Decision Models
H04V5A.content: This course discusses the basic deterministic techniques of operational research. In particular attention is spent on linear and integral programming. Particularly the choice and construction of models are discussed and the role of the computer and modern optimization software are illustrated on the basis of numerous examples (small exercises and practical studies), both during the lectures and during the practical sessions. Following topics are discussed: structure of linear models, the simplex method, sensitivity analysis, transport and allocation models, network models, integral and combinatorial programming. Apart from optimal procedures (simple and multiple aims) much attention goes to heuristic solution procedures. The main means of support is the LINDO/LINGO package.
H04V5A.learningOutcomes: The student should be able to model a problem in a mathematical way, find the proper solution method and discuss the results taking certain assumptions into account.
H04V5A.evaluation: The exam is written and open book. Students are allowed to use the course material (book, exercises, lecture notes,...) during the exam.

H04V6A.name: Introduction to Operational Management and Logistics
H04V6A.content: The course consists of several chapters discussing: what is operations management and logistics: overview, links and trends; forecasting; aggregate production planning; inventory management for end items; production and inventory control systems such as MRP, JIT, TOC; conclusions.
H04V6A.learningOutcomes: The student is able to model an operations management and logistics problem, make the proper assumptions, propose and apply a solution method and to discuss the results.
H04V6A.prerequisites: Knowledge on operations research and basic economics.
H04V6A.evaluation: Type: Exam during the examination period. Assessment method: Written. Type of questions: Open questions, Closed questions. Permitted materials: List of formulas, Calculator.
H04V6A.teachingMethods: Interactive ex cathedra lectures + exercises during class.

H04W0A.name: Production Machines and Systems
H04W0A.content: The course comprises the following chapters: Concepts for production machines and systems; Construction of machine tools (building forms, materials, construction..); Tool spindles (construction, drives, tool holder systems); Clamping, slides.. (guides, drives, positioning systems..); Controllers (PLC, NC programming, "feature-based" controls, communications, adaptive control); Flexible production systems (integration of machines, palletizing, communication between machines..); Thermal stability of machine tools; Dynamic behavior of machine tools; Quality control of machine tools.
H04W0A.learningOutcomes: The student knows and learns how modern production machines and/or systems are constructed. The student can explain the role and function of the different components (frames, guides, actuators, control, etc.) of an existing machine or system (based on a real machine or a drawing/model).
H04W0A.prerequisites: Basic knowledge of machine construction (machine elements), production techniques and materials.
H04W0A.evaluation: Type: Exam during the examination period. Assessment method: Oral. Type of questions: Open questions. Permitted materials: None. Closed book exam. Lab session attendance is compulsory.
H04W0A.teachingMethods: Classical lectures! The teacher covers the material using PowerPoint presentations, supplemented by notes on the blackboard.

H04W6A.name: Aircraft Performance and Stability
H04W6A.content: Part I: Performance - introduction, equations of motion in a vertical plane, glide, level flight, climb, range and endurance, turns, take-off and landing. Part II: static stability and control - aerodynamic characteristics, longitudinal/directional/lateral stability, control surfaces. Part III: Equations of motion and dynamic stability - reference frames, force/moment equations, linear model derivation.
H04W6A.learningOutcomes: The student is able to calculate aircraft performances related to the complete flight profile based on simplifying assumptions and approximate empirical relations. The student is able to formulate the requirements for static stability and determine required control surface deflections. The student is able to derive a linearised dynamic model for control purposes starting from dynamic equations of an aircraft.
H04W6A.prerequisites: Basic mechanics, aerodynamics and system theory as introduced in the subjects 'Toegepaste mechanica: deel1', 'Toegepaste Mechanica: deel 2', 'Aerodynamica' and 'Systeemtheorie' or equivalent.
H04W6A.evaluation: Type: Exam during the examination period. Assessment method: Written. Part I and II: exam consists of problems related to performance and static stability. Part III: exam consists of problems and theoretical derivations related to dynamic stability. Students may use an approved list of formulas and have access to Matlab.

H04X0A.name: Structural Dynamics, Analysis and Numerical Modelling
H04X0A.content: Part 1: Identification and use of structural dynamic models (Modal testing) covering SDOF/MDOF vibrations, signal processing, FRF identification, instrumentation, excitation techniques, parameter identification, model validation, sensitivity analysis, structural modification, and model updating. Part 2: Finite element models for structural dynamic analysis covering modelling considerations, solution methods, and model reduction techniques.
H04X0A.learningOutcomes: The student acquires theoretical and practical insight in the process of determining the dynamics of a mechanical system by experiments and/or numerical analysis. Students can determine dynamic characteristics through experimental modal analysis and numerical modelling, interpret results, combine approaches, use state-of-the-art tools, and report on dynamic analysis projects including literature surveys.
H04X0A.prerequisites: The students should have sufficient knowledge of mechanical vibrations, system theory, sensors and measuring systems and numerical modelling.
H04X0A.evaluation: Three parts: permanent evaluation via project (3/20 points, required to pass); written and oral reporting about project (15/20 points); and literature survey (2/20 points, required to pass). Assessment methods include participation, presentation, and reports with open questions.

H04X2A.name: Project Management
H04X2A.content: Introduction; Organisational structures and task allocation; Project planning; Project budget; Management of resources; Project control; Computer support for project management; Project termination; Case studies
H04X2A.learningOutcomes: The aim of this course is to provide the student with an overview of techniques and means that are available for the start up, execution, follow up and adjustment of large projects.
H04X2A.prerequisites: Access to a familiar project case (e.g. thesis project) is required in view of the evaluation format which is based on a case study. A possible course on business administration in the curriculum can best be scheduled before attending this course.
H04X2A.evaluation: Assignment per two students with presentation and defense (oral exam) during exam session. Exam timing is coordinated per team of students.

H04X3A.name: Control Theory
H04X3A.content: Introduction to least-squares time domain system identification; Linearization of nonlinear systems; Introduction to control systems; Basic properties of feedback systems; Performance of feedback systems; Root locus analysis and design; Frequency-response based compensator design; State feedback based compensator design; Optimal control (LQR) and optimal estimation (Kalman filter)
H04X3A.learningOutcomes: The student is able to apply the basic time-domain system identification procedure for linear time-invariant systems with one input and one output... linearize a nonlinear system... design a classical compensator using frequency-domain methods... design a compensator based on state-feedback, including a closed-loop state estimator... add feed forward to a compensator to eliminate steady-state errors... design a Kalman filter to estimate the states of a linear or nonlinear system optimally.
H04X3A.prerequisites: Solving linear differential and difference equations with constant coefficients; Fourier series and transform; Complex function theory; Solving systems of linear equations; Elementary matrix calculus; Eigenvalues and eigenvectors; Frequency domain analysis of discrete- and continuous-time systems; Sampling of signals; Transformation between system models
H04X3A.evaluation: Continuous assessment without exam during the examination period. Assessment method: Report. Students work in groups of two on a project consisting of four assignments. A separate report must be submitted for each assignment. Each report counts for 25% of the total score.

H04X3B.name: Systems and Control Theory
H04X3B.content: Introduction to least-squares time domain system identification; Linearization of nonlinear systems; Introduction to control systems; Basic properties of feedback systems; Performance of feedback systems; Root locus analysis and design; Frequency-response based compensator design; State feedback based compensator design; Optimal control (LQR) and optimal estimation (Kalman filter)
H04X3B.learningOutcomes: Students will apply time-domain system identification, linearize nonlinear systems, analyze continuous and discrete systems in time and frequency domains, design classical and state-feedback compensators, and design Kalman filters for optimal state estimation.
H04X3B.prerequisites: Solving linear differential and difference equations with constant coefficients in time and frequency domain; basic knowledge of Fourier series and Fourier transform; complex function theory; applied linear algebra; solving systems of linear equations; elementary matrix operations; eigenvalues and eigenvectors
H04X3B.evaluation: Report, Written. Consists of two parts: exercise exam on systems theory (2/7 of evaluation) and project-based evaluation for control theory (5/7). Systems theory: closed-book written exam with formulary. Control theory: four assignments submitted as separate reports, each counting 25%.

H04X5A.name: Spacecraft Technology and Space Environment
H04X5A.content: Covers five main areas: introduction to aerospace history, orbital mechanics including Kepler orbits and perturbations, propulsion and rocket systems, satellite construction and subsystems, and space environment factors including microgravity, radiation, and space debris.
H04X5A.learningOutcomes: Being able to evaluate the different elements of an aerospace missions: launching, orbital mechanics and corrections, performing the mission requirements during the lifetime of a spacecraft.
H04X5A.prerequisites: SIMULTANEOUS(H04U3A) AND SIMULTANEOUS(H04S6A) AND SIMULTANEOUS(H03Y1A) AND SIMULTANEOUS(H04P9A) AND SIMULTANEOUS(H04X7A)
H04X5A.evaluation: Type: Exam during the examination period. Assessment method: Oral

H04X7A.name: Sensors and Measurements Systems
H04X7A.content: Statistical and dynamic characteristics of measuring systems, Accuracy and pressure effects, Signals and noise in measuring systems, Recorders, Signal conditioning systems, Signal processing systems, Data-reading systems, Flow measurements, Warmth-effects in measuring systems, Optical measuring systems, Ultrasonic measuring systems, Data-acquisition systems
H04X7A.learningOutcomes: The student can build a measuring system for frequently occurring mechanical measurement problems by selecting or designing the appropriate measuring system components.
H04X7A.prerequisites: The student is supposed to have followed an introductory course in electrotechnology, dynamics and vibrations, systemtheory and control technology.
H04X7A.evaluation: Participation during contact hours, Practical exam, Written exam with Open questions, Closed questions
H04X7A.lecturer: Gryllias Konstantinos, Swevers Jan, Vetrano Maria Rosaria (Coordinator)

H04Y2A.name: Reliability of Mechanical Systems
H04Y2A.content: Students are challenged to apply their knowledge on engineering mechanics in the context of reliability, focusing on design, production as well as maintenance of mechanical systems. Topics include general reliability introduction, basic elements, system reliability, analysis methods (FMECA, risk analysis, event/failure tree analysis), reliability in design, and mechanical reliability in micro-electronics.
H04Y2A.learningOutcomes: Students should know and understand the meaning of standard terminology in reliability analysis techniques and be able to select distribution types, analyze testing data, quantify system reliability, apply Markov process modeling, and describe qualitative/semi-quantitative techniques. Additionally, they should understand strength-load interference, reliability indices, and reliability-based design optimization principles.
H04Y2A.prerequisites: Basic knowledge on statistics, more specifically probability distributions and probability theory, is required. Basic knowledge of continuum mechanics, more specifically stress conditions in materials under external loading, is required.
H04Y2A.evaluation: Oral, Written exam with Open questions. Students may bring an own, hand-written formularium (max 1 A4 recto-verso, mathematical equations only). Seminar evaluation based on student reports and attendance.

H04Y6A.name: Turbomachinery, Part 2
H04Y6A.content: Course topics: axial and radial turbomachines with non-compressible and compressible flows and the network on which the machine is installed.
H04Y6A.learningOutcomes: Offering an area in which fluid mechanics are the driving force in the detailed study of turbomachines. Improving integrated thinking and making the applications understandable by pointing out and using other disciplines.
H04Y6A.prerequisites: Basic knowledge of Turbomachines and Aerodynamics.
H04Y6A.evaluation: Type: Exam during the examination period. Assessment method: Oral

H04Y7A.name: Turbulence
H04Y7A.content: Origin of turbulence, properties, chaos; Equations for fluid flow, vorticity equations; Statistical description, correlations and spectra, averaged flow equations; Turbulence at high Reynolds numbers: isotropy, equilibrium theory, K41 theory, intermittency; Anisotropy; Free shear flows, mixing layers, jets, wakes; Boundary-layer turbulence, law of the wall; Simulation of turbulent flows: DNS, LES, RANS, DES; Turbulence modelling for RANS, LES, DES
H04Y7A.learningOutcomes: The student is able to explain the physical phenomena which play a role in turbulent flows, and can give an overview of the most important simulation techniques, and analytical tools for the description of turbulence.
H04Y7A.prerequisites: Good knowledge of fluid mechanics, and numerical modelling
H04Y7A.evaluation: Exam during the examination period. Assessment method: Oral. Type of questions: Open questions. Permitted materials: Course material, Reference work. The exam is partially a classical open-book exam, with questions on the subject of turbulence. Next to that, students discuss their review of a recent scientific paper.

H04Z5A.name: Thermochemische conversie
H04Z5A.content: Deze cursus bespreekt de thermische, chemische en fluïdummechanische aspecten van thermochemische conversie, met focus op verbranding, vergassing en pyrolyse.
H04Z5A.learningOutcomes: De student verwerft vaardigheden inzake ingenieursmatige berekeningen van thermochemische conversie (verbranding, vergassing, pyrolyse).
H04Z5A.prerequisites: De student kan werken met de begrippen uit de thermodynamica, warmteoverdracht en stromingsleer en kan in deze disciplines zelfstandig oefeningen oplossen. Beginvoorwaarden: Bachelor in de ingenieurswetenschappen
H04Z5A.evaluation: Type: Examen tijdens de examenperiode. Evaluatievorm: Schriftelijk. Vraagvormen: Open vragen
H04Z5A.teachingMethods: Deze cursus wordt gedoceerd in de vorm van hoorcolleges. Tijdens de hoorcolleges wordt van de studenten verwacht dat ze actief luisteren en meedenken.

H04Z8A.name: Aircraft Engines
H04Z8A.content: Thermodynamic study of turbo engines, performance and optimizations, areas of use, future developments. Operation of the parts as elements of the turbo engine, inlets, compressors, combustion chambers, turbines, exhausts.
H04Z8A.learningOutcomes: To acquire a scientific in-depth knowledge of the operation of gas turbines, turbo jet engines, turbo propulsors and their main components.
H04Z8A.evaluation: Exam during the examination period. Assessment method: Oral

H05T6A.name: Satellite Navigation and Communications
H05T6A.content: The course covers 9 lectures including: radionavigation history, satellite navigation systems, orbits and reference systems, signals, measurement errors, receiver implementations, position estimation, industry trends, and guest speaker sessions. Additionally, there are 4 lab sessions where students work with MATLAB software-defined radio receivers to grab RF samples, process data, and calculate positions.
H05T6A.learningOutcomes: Students should understand GNSS systems like GPS and Galileo, apply mathematical concepts to radionavigation problems, understand measurement errors, and have an overview of the radiolocation ecosystem. At the end, the students should be able to: Understand how GPS/GNSS work in some depth. Develop satnav receiver algorithms and applications and analyse their performance.
H05T6A.prerequisites: Basic knowhow of digital communications and antennas are assumed: Electromagnetism and electromagnetic wave propagation; Components of communication systems... Phase and amplitude modulation techniques; Standard multiple access techniques including FDMA, TDMA, CDMA
H05T6A.evaluation: 80% individual closed-book test: Short problems and questions based on the lectured material. 20% laboratory work and presentation.

H05V3A.name: Vliegtuigconstructies
H05V3A.content: Topics include aircraft loading, stress analysis of primary components, structural instability assessment, fatigue life calculations using fracture mechanics, and finite element modeling. Covers static analysis, dynamic effects, flutter, and practical design considerations for wing boxes, fuselages, and reinforced panels.
H05V3A.learningOutcomes: Students will understand mechanical loads on aircraft structures, conduct stress analysis on primary components, assess instability risks, perform fatigue calculations using fracture mechanics, and develop finite element models to analyze aircraft components.
H05V3A.prerequisites: begrippen van de elasticiteitsleer (concepts of elasticity theory); methoden voor spanningsanalyse in staven, balken en platen (stress analysis methods for rods, beams, and plates); basisvaardigheden voor simulatie m.b.v. commerciële software voor eindige elementen (basic finite element simulation skills).
H05V3A.evaluation: Mondeling, Schriftelijk (Oral and Written). Three questions with unequal weighting: one major question on global stress analysis of aircraft components, two smaller questions on detailed component analysis. Two questions discussed orally, one written only.

H06U6A.name: Dutch Language and Cultures
H06U6A.learningOutcomes: The main aim of this course is to help students acquire basic communicative skills in Dutch (level A1 of the Common European Framework).
H06U6A.evaluation: There will be a test (writing, speaking and reading) at the end of the course as well as a number of assignments during the course.

H06U9B.name: Advanced Robot Control Systems
H06U9B.content: The following aspects of robot systems are introduced: kinematics and dynamics, control, task and motion specification, sensor-based world perception and task execution monitoring.
H06U9B.learningOutcomes: Students will learn what are the fundamental components of advanced robot control systems, and how the robot must/can interact with its environment, and with the task it has to perform.
H06U9B.prerequisites: (SIMULTANEOUS(H04P5A) AND (FLEXIBLE(H04X3A) OR FLEXIBLE(H04X3B))) OR (SIMULTANEOUS(H00R9A) AND (FLEXIBLE(H00S3A) OR FLEXIBLE(H00S4A))). As a baseline, this course expects students to be familiar with beginning Master-level basics of engineering systems: control theory, kinematics, dynamics, programming, probability theory.
H06U9B.evaluation: Continuous assessment without exam during the examination period, using Paper/Project, Participation during contact hours, Presentation, Take-Home.

H08K0A.name: Safety of Chemical and Biological Products and of Chemical Processes
H08K0A.content: Intrinsic hazards of chemical products (e.g., toxicity, flammability, etc.) and biological product (e.g., pathogenicity); Classification & Labelling (e.g., CLP); Preventive measures (e.g., PPE); REACH for hazardous chemicals; Hazard evaluation and risk assessment methods including DOW FEI, FMEA, HAZOP; Safety aspects during project engineering.
H08K0A.learningOutcomes: Identify and judge risks with respect to your own work/the work of the people you supervise when working in the chemical industry; determine the necessary measures to exclude or reduce risks to an acceptable level; identify and assess hazards; understand hazard vectors; retrieve product hazard information; interpret hazardous product information like SDS; understand classification/labeling and REACH principles; know differences between chemical and biological product safety; and apply risk analysis methods like HAZOP and QRA.
H08K0A.evaluation: Product safety assignment counts for 40% (8 out of 20) of the final score. The written exam on process safety counts for 60% (12 out of 20). Open book exam permitted with course materials and personal notes.

H08N0A.name: Introduction to Safety Engineering
H08N0A.content: Some important major accidents in the process industries are used as starting point to prove the importance of safety engineering and as a starting point to explain the principles of the international regulations (e.g. Seveso directive) and risk assessment methods. Topics include hazard versus risk, process safety, risk analysis techniques, inherent safe design, Seveso directive principles, and human factors.
H08N0A.learningOutcomes: Students will understand orders of magnitude of incidents, define safety and risk vocabulary, understand risk perception principles, distinguish safety from security, know risk analysis techniques, define inherent safe design and business continuity, understand the Seveso directive, comprehend process safety management, analyze historical incidents, understand human and organizational factors, conduct risk assessments, and create a build-in safety reflex in the actual and future activities in the individual, professional and societal context.
H08N0A.evaluation: Part 1 (Lectures): Written exam during exam period. Closed book. Part 2 (Seminars): Written exam during exam period. Closed book.

H08P2A.name: Safety Aspects of Industrial Installations
H08P2A.learningOutcomes: The aim is to create insight in the diverse technical safety problems in industry in order to allow the safety engineer to recognize the risks and to take the necessary measures to control them.
H08P2A.evaluation: The evaluation covers the three parts of course: thermal, electrical and mechanical installations. The exam is a closed book exam. Each course part is evaluated and the arithmetic mean is taken to compute the final course score.
H08P2A.teachingMethods: Components include lectures (8 hours each for thermal, mechanical, electrical), seminars/practicals (6 hours each), company visits to power plants and chemical plants, and hands-on risk assessment seminars in machinery lab.
H08P2A.lecturer: Bernaerts Kristel (Coordinator), Brouwers Bert, Vanwynsberghe Frank

H09J2A.name: Image Analysis and Understanding
H09J2A.content: Part I: Image processing - recording and display, sampling and quantization, filtering and image enhancement, unitary transforms (2D FFT, PCA). Part II: Image interpretation - surface features (color, texture), optical flow and tracking, 3D geometry and reconstruction, local features and image matching. Part III: Machine-learning based approaches - network architectures for image classification, dense prediction tasks (semantic segmentation, depth estimation, pose estimation), object detection, advanced topics (image generation, dealing with video, efficient implementations, new trends, ...)
H09J2A.learningOutcomes: Conceptual knowledge of basic algorithms for the processing and interpretation of images.
H09J2A.prerequisites: The student must have a basic knowledge of algebra, analysis, geometry, signal processing, pattern recognition and basic notions of machine learning.
H09J2A.evaluation: Exam during the examination period. Assessment method: Oral. Type of questions: Multiple choice. Students get a set of multiple choice questions. After a short preparation, they are asked to explain and motivate their choices during the oral exam, sometimes followed by a short discussion.
H09J2A.teachingMethods: 18 lecture classes: roughly 1/3 on image processing, 1/3 on image interpretation, and 1/3 on machine-learning based methods. Guided exercises, partially computer-supported.
H09J2A.language: English (Dutch-speaking students can take the exam in Dutch if they want to.)

H09P4A.name: Engineering & Entrepreneurship
H09P4A.learningOutcomes: The course explains and illustrates the role of leadership and technology in the entrepreneurial process. Students will be able to explain technology's role in entrepreneurship, leverage market opportunities through resource planning, create business plans, understand company positioning, explain product development cycles, and identify Business Strategic Dialogue techniques.
H09P4A.prerequisites: Students are not allowed to follow the course H09Q1A 'Leadership and Strategic Management' (3 ECTS) nor H04V2A 'Ontwerpmethodologieën' (6 ECTS) when they subscribe this course.
H09P4A.evaluation: Continuous assessment for Business Simulations based on participation; written exams with open questions for Strategic Management and Creativity modules; short paper for Technology & Entrepreneurship case studies. Participation in all components is mandatory.
H09P4A.teachingMethods: Interactive business simulation games (mandatory attendance), mixture of classes and seminars, lectures.
H09P4A.lecturer: Duflou Joost (Coordinator), De Moor Bart, Geldof Bernard, Gorissen Benjamin, Joubert Johan

H09Q1A.name: Leadership and Strategic Management
H09Q1A.learningOutcomes: Students are able to apply what they have learned in OLA1 and OLA2: define a vision, formulate a strategy and objectives, organize themselves in teams and a proper functional structure. Additional objectives include analyzing situations, understanding Business Strategic Dialogues, implementing business strategy communication, and recognizing relationships between team objectives, evaluation, and rewarding.
H09Q1A.prerequisites: Basic knowledge on industrial engineering (production planning), management accounting and economics. Also requires simultaneous enrollment in course H04D9A (Psychological and Social Aspects of the Management of Organisations).
H09Q1A.evaluation: Participation during contact hours, Presentation, Written assessments. Strategic Management component uses a written exam; Business Simulations component evaluated on cooperation and presentation.
H09Q1A.teachingMethods: Interactive business simulation games: presence is obligatory. Mixture of classes and seminars.
H09Q1A.lecturer: Duflou Joost (Coordinator), Geldof Bernard, Joubert Johan

H09Z9A.name: Master's Thesis
H09Z9A.content: The master's thesis contains an in-depth study of a topic from the specialization engineering programme. This study can be purely theoretical or a mixture of theory and experiment.
H09Z9A.learningOutcomes: The thesis serves as the capstone, integrating all aspects of the Master of Mechanical Engineering. Students develop capabilities including: literature review, formulating research questions, selecting appropriate methodologies, conducting original research, applying advanced knowledge, problem-solving, validating results, academic communication, professional collaboration, critical reflection, sustainability/ethics considerations, and scientific integrity.
H09Z9A.prerequisites: You may only take this course if you only need to acquire a maximum of 72 credits to obtain the diploma.
H09Z9A.evaluation: Continuous assessment without exam during the examination period via Paper/Project, Participation during contact hours, Presentation. Evaluation covers three aspects: process (personal contribution, professionalism), product (research quality, originality, methodology), and reporting (text, presentation, insight, discussion). All three must meet expectations to pass.

H0A13A.name: Dredging Technology for Mechanical Engineers
H0A13A.content: 1. Introduction to dredging; 2. Dredging equipment (TSHD, CSD, BHD); 3. Hydraulic transport; 4. Dredging projects; 5. Project Acquisition
H0A13A.learningOutcomes: The course aims to provide the participants an insight in the technical, economical and sustainability aspects of dredging projects and equipment.
H0A13A.prerequisites: (FLEXIBLE(H08W4A) OR FLEXIBLE(H0H49A)) where H08W4A is Fluïdummechanica and H0H49A is Hydraulica. Entry requirement: Hydraulics/Fluid Mechanics and drives.
H0A13A.evaluation: Type: Exam during the examination period. Assessment method: Written. Type of questions: Multiple choice, Open questions. Permitted materials: Calculator.
H0A13A.lecturer: Fordeyn Jan, Nees Tom (Coordinator: Nees Tom)

H0A15A.name: Virtual Product Development
H0A15A.content: Part I - Advanced CAD: Geometric modeling, modeling methods (CSG, B-rep, voxel-based, STL), parametric and feature modeling, assembly modeling, tolerances, data exchange, virtual reality, and CAD-CAE integration. Part 2 - Selection Process: process selection based on shape types, DFM design, cost estimation.
H0A15A.learningOutcomes: Students know advanced modeling principles including parametric and feature modeling; can make initial process selection for machining based on constraints; know CAD data exchange methods and can evaluate transfer quality.
H0A15A.prerequisites: Basic CAD experience and knowledge of manufacturing processes. If no basic CAD experience is available, additional exercises are requested at course start.
H0A15A.evaluation: Report (20%) and oral examination (80%) during examination period. Students present a CAD model, short report (5-10 pages), and discuss modeling principles, process selection, data exchange quality, and course content integration.
H0A15A.teachingMethods: Classical lectures using PowerPoint presentations supplemented by blackboard notes; independent student work on guided exercises with assistant support.

H0A21A.name: Two-Phase Flow: Theory and Applications
H0A21A.content: Introduction to two-phase flows: Solid-liquid and gas–liquid flows; Fundamentals of pool boiling and forced boiling; Atomization and sprays; Two-phase flow application
H0A21A.learningOutcomes: Based on a description of the physical phenomena occurring, the students develop models and build up knowledge on the validity of empirical correlations. Through a critical view on existing correlations, the students choose the right empirical correlations for a real design problem, motivate their choice, being aware of the limitations, and using the course text and the literature.
H0A21A.prerequisites: Basics of heat transfer (conduction, convection and radiation) and fluid flow.
H0A21A.evaluation: Continuous assessment without exam during the examination period. Assessment method: Presentation, Report. The final presentation counts for 30% of the total score; the final reporting counts for 70% of the total score.
H0A21A.teachingMethods: Guided self-education: independently processing the course text with often occurring guidance sessions on a certain part of the course, in which specific aspects, questions or problems will be dealt with.

H0E62A.name: Advanced Subtractive Manufacturing
H0E62A.content: Dynamic aspects of machining (high speed machining, chatter); 5-axis machining; Machining of hard and difficult-to-machine materials using conventional, non-conventional (e.g. EDM, ECM, LBM,…) and hybrid processes; Micro-machining and surface texturing; Advanced abrasive processes
H0E62A.learningOutcomes: Encompasses understanding fundamental principles of material removal processes, explaining process condition influences, estimating process outcomes in efficiency and quality, and proposing innovative sustainable machining strategies.
H0E62A.prerequisites: Basic knowledge of production processes: Productietechnieken en –systemen (or equivalent)
H0E62A.evaluation: Exam during the examination period. Assessment method: Oral, with Open questions, Closed questions; Calculator permitted. Lab session evaluations are incorporated into final grades.

H0E64A.name: Additive Manufacturing Processes - 3D Printing
H0E64A.content: The lectures will be organized in two parts. In the first part, the general concept of 3D printing will be discussed after which students will learn the basic working principles of the most important 3D printing technologies for processing polymers, metals and ceramics.
H0E64A.learningOutcomes: Understand the basic working principles of the different 3D printing technologies for printing polymer, metal or ceramic components, and the hardware and software involved
H0E64A.prerequisites: Basic knowledge of physics, chemistry, materials science and manufacturing techniques is required.
H0E64A.evaluation: Written exam with oral explanation. Type: Exam during examination period; Assessment method: Oral, Written; Question types: Multiple choice, Open questions, Closed questions
H0E64A.teachingMethods: Lectures (20 hours) and Lab Sessions (5 hours), including lab sessions in the KU Leuven Additive Manufacturing lab, seminars, company visits

H0E66A.name: Advanced Measurement Techniques in Fluid Mechanics
H0E66A.content: Topics include hot wire velocimetry, Laser Doppler Velocimetry, Particle Image Velocimetry, PIV-based techniques, Laser Induced Fluorescence techniques, optical density measurements, and high-speed visualization with image analysis algorithms.
H0E66A.learningOutcomes: The student acquires skills concerning advanced measurement techniques such as Hot Wire Velocimetry, Particle Image Velocimetry, Laser Doppler Velocimetry, Imagery and Fluorescence techniques. The student learns how to process data, how to critically analyse the data and extract relevant physical quantities.
H0E66A.evaluation: The grading consists of two parts: The final presentation counts for 30% of the total score; The final reporting counts for 50% of the total score; Laboratory attitude and skills count for 20%
H0E66A.teachingMethods: Lectures (1.2 ECTS, 8 hours) and Lab Sessions (1.8 ECTS, 20 hours)

H0E68B.name: Production and Quality Assurance Processes in the Aerospace Industry
H0E68B.content: Covers Advanced Subtractive Manufacturing topics including dynamic aspects of machining (high speed machining, chatter) and 5-axis machining, plus Quality Assurance covering quality control procedures and production cell structure.
H0E68B.learningOutcomes: Understand the fundamental working principles of different conventional and non-conventional material removal processes; Explain the influence of the process conditions on the material removal mechanisms and properties of the final product.
H0E68B.prerequisites: Basic knowledge of production processes: Productietechnieken en –systemen (or equivalent)
H0E68B.evaluation: Oral exam during the examination period, with Open questions, Closed questions permitted. Final mark calculated as geometric mean over both course parts.
H0E68B.teachingMethods: Lectures, lab sessions (practical work on 5-axis machining and EDM), practice sessions, and an industrial visit with professional presentations.

H0E70A.name: Vehicle Propulsion
H0E70A.content: Transmission and power split operation and design; ICE-electric hybrid powertrains; System level simulation methods for powertrain design
H0E70A.learningOutcomes: The student has to be able to name and explain (reproduce) the concepts and thinking patterns around the different aspects of vehicle propulsion, and integrate knowledge of combustion engines, transmission lines and vehicles
H0E70A.prerequisites: The student knows how to work with concepts of combustion engine theory, electricity, machine construction, control theory, system theory and mathematical analysis (specific course requirements listed: H01N8A, H01L8A, H01N0A, and Master-level Mechanical Drives and Control Theory)
H0E70A.evaluation: Exam during the examination period via Written assessment with Open questions; cooperation during lab sessions is evaluated
H0E70A.teachingMethods: Lectures (20 hours) and Practical/Lab Sessions (5 hours)

H0E73A.name: Stage studiebegeleiding: Werktuigkunde
H0E73A.content: Students serve as peer tutors in exercise sessions or practicals for Applied Mechanics 1, Applied Mechanics 2, and Thermodynamics, facilitating interactive learning through explanation, examples, guided questioning, discussion stimulation, feedback provision, and student encouragement.
H0E73A.learningOutcomes: De student-begeleider kan de leerinhouden kort en bondig uitleggen, toelichten en verdedigen, plus nine additional specific competencies including facilitating student learning, using teaching aids effectively, maintaining an empathetic attitude, managing groups, and reflecting on performance.
H0E73A.prerequisites: De student moet in het bezit zijn van het bachelordiploma en moet credits hebben behaald voor het opleidingsonderdeel waarvoor hij/zij als student-begeleider zal optreden.
H0E73A.evaluation: Permanente evaluatie zonder examen, using observation during minimum 2 sessions, self-evaluation via reflection forms, and peer discussion. Grading is pass/fail; not calculated toward degree classification.
H0E73A.teachingMethods: Three-phase structure: preparation phase, execution phase during sessions, and reflection phase; roles include explaining content, providing examples, posing guiding questions, and encouraging participation.
H0E73A.lecturer: Baelmans Tine, Desmet Wim, Vandepitte Dirk, Vander Sloten Jos

H0H00A.name: Thermal Systems
