H0H00A.content: Thermal systems are treated from demand side to supply side in the global energy picture, covering refrigeration systems, heat pump dynamics, building clusters, pinch analysis, and thermal power plants including CHP and conventional systems.
H0H00A.learningOutcomes: Students can analyze thermal systems statically and dynamically, investigate dynamic behavior using time scales, improve system performance through component interaction, choose appropriate systems for sustainable energy conversion, and understand design-control impacts.
H0H00A.prerequisites: The course is open to students with a thorough knowledge of thermal engineering, such as Technical Thermodynamics, Heat Transfer, Fluid Mechanics and Turbomachines.
H0H00A.evaluation: Written exam during the examination period with multiple choice, open and closed questions; calculator permitted. Insights from lab sessions may be included.
H0H00A.teachingMethods: Lectures (32 hours) and practical sessions including exercise sessions and take-home exercises applying lecture material.

H0N82A.name: Religions
H0N82A.content: Key themes in religion and theology are presented, based on insights of modern social sciences and contemporary philosophical thinking.
H0N82A.learningOutcomes: Students aim at clarifying the functioning of religions and world views, especially the Christian religion, into culture and society
H0N82A.prerequisites: This course does not require specific prior knowledge. General knowledge of the main lines of philosophy, ethics and western culture and history do belong to the presupposed background
H0N82A.evaluation: Type: Exam during the examination period. Assessment method: Written. Type of questions: Multiple choice
H0N82A.teachingMethods: Interactive college. Apart from the lectures, a guest lecture could be organized.

H0O78A.name: Vehicle Systems
H0O78A.content: Overview of mechatronic systems in a vehicle; Drive line in road vehicles: manual/automatic transmission, 4WD, power management; Passive safety in road vehicles: crash-tests, regulations, airbag, crash warning; Active safety in road vehicles: ABS-EBM - ASC; Transport control in railroad vehicles; Homologation
H0O78A.learningOutcomes: Acquiring insight into and knowledge on the functional part of the different subsystems of a vehicle and their coherence, with attention for mechatronic aspects.
H0O78A.prerequisites: Knowledge of machine construction, control theory, drives, kinematics and dynamics.
H0O78A.evaluation: Continuous assessment without exam during the examination period. Assessment method: Paper/Project, Presentation. Report and presentation on the mechatronic and technical aspects of a recent vehicle system.

H0O79A.name: Dimensional Metrology
H0O79A.content: Fundamentals of dimensional metrology and quality control; 1D measurement; 2D measurement; 3D digital coordinates measurement; Special techniques: optical measuring techniques (laser) interferometry, X-ray CT metrology.
H0O79A.learningOutcomes: To provide knowledge of the basic principles and techniques used for dimensional quality control in companies.
H0O79A.evaluation: Written exam during the examination period with open questions. Permitted materials: Course material, Calculator
H0O79A.teachingMethods: Lectures (33 hours) and Labs and seminars with dimensional measuring machines: coordinate measuring machines, roughness meters, optical measurement techniques, etc.

H0O81A.name: New Energy Technologies: Seminars
H0O81A.content: The topics covered are new technologies that present themselves in the field of thermoelectric technology or energy.
H0O81A.learningOutcomes: The student must be able to recognize the application of thermo-technical sciences in the design of new thermoelectric systems and describe it academically.
H0O81A.prerequisites: Knowledge of the following disciplines: thermal systems, thermodynamics, heat transfer, fluid mechanics, combustion, general mechanics, control engineering.
H0O81A.evaluation: Continuous assessment without exam during the examination period. Assessment method: Presentation, Report, Self assessment/Peer assessment

H0O82A.name: Precision Engineering
H0O82A.content: 1) Status of the technology: Technology trends, Moore's Law, Law of Taniguchi 2) Design principles: Axiom of minimum information, principle of functional independence, Total Design, Avoiding play, Principle of Abbe, design on stiffness, minimization of thermal deformation, Generation of precise movements, kinematic design, Error Correction, Filter principle, The reduction principle. 3) Processing Principles, Upper limit of the machining accuracy, Principle of element technology, the concept of "processing unit", the copy principle, the evolution principle, the principle of Abbe, workpiece material, Distorsion free chucking, machining in several steps, in-situ machining.
H0O82A.learningOutcomes: Analyze and apply the basic principles of the design and manufacture of high-and ultra precision machines and instruments.
H0O82A.prerequisites: Knowledge (basic course followed) required on optical waves, mechanical engineering, production engineering.
H0O82A.evaluation: Partial or continuous assessment with (final) exam during the examination period. Assessment method: Oral, Paper/Project. Type of questions: Open questions. Permitted materials: Computer.
H0O82A.teachingMethods: Lectures with illustrations of construction and operation principles. Laboratory visits to discuss applications.

H0O83A.name: Design of Optics
H0O83A.content: Introduction Geometrical optics; lenses, mirrors etc…, this part have to be aquired by self study due to it's basic nature Electro-magnetic waves, maxwell equations, wave equation. Waves through media, dispersion effects Reflection and refraction, Schnell's law, Fresnel expressions of reflection and refraction on electrical isolators, effect on polarization of the light. Interferance and bending on optical gratings, spectral resolution Polarization, polarizing components such as polaroid films, nichol prisms etc.. Doppler effect The human eye, color vision, displays Interferometry, different types in interferometers, laser-doppler interferometry, their applications, analysis of optical components such as beam splitters, quarter and half lamda plates, etc… electro-optic components such as Braggs cells, Pocket cells.
H0O83A.learningOutcomes: Optics find its apllications in many domains of engineering, for example data storage and communications, precision measurements, camera's, displays, production techniques etc…The electro-magnetic nature of optical waves is of prime importance to understand how an optical application functions. The student must gather this knowledge and be able to apply it in optical designs.
H0O83A.prerequisites: Knowledge (basic course followed) required on optical waves, mechanical engineering, production engineering. Physics course on optics.
H0O83A.evaluation: Partial or continuous assessment with (final) exam during the examination period. Take-Home. Open questions. Permitted materials: Course material, Computer

H0R71A.name: Design Methodologies
H0R71A.content: 1. Introduction: survey design cycle, characteristics of design processes, course structure. 2. Pre-trajectory: Identification of needs, Creating a product portfolio, Problem definition. 3. Marketing concepts and market analysis. 4. The preparation of design specifications, including information sources: Standards, IP preconditions and patent literature. 5. Creativity Methods: i.a. Lateral thinking, Brainstorming, Synectics, Biomimicry, Combinatorial concept generation, Morphological analysis, TRIZ. 6. Decision making and design evaluation methods: Design axioms, Decision tables, Decision theory, Multi-criteria analysis. 7. Material selection and optimization. 8. User Oriented Design: QFD, Value Analysis. 9. Production Oriented Design: Design for manufacturing methods. 10. Ecodesign and Life Cycle Engineering. 11. Life cycle costing and product service systems. 12. Prototyping: methods and techniques. 13. Case studies
H0R71A.learningOutcomes: After completing this course the student possesses the analytic skills and has mastered the methods for a systematic design approach. Specifically, the student can describe the procedures and techniques available for the studied design methods, select the appropriate methods and apply the related techniques to concrete examples.
H0R71A.prerequisites: Participants preferentially have initial experience with design projects (P&Os).
H0R71A.evaluation: Closed book, oral exam with written preparation during the exam period. Grading of group reports resulting from work sessions (group project)

H0R73A.name: Forming Technology
H0R73A.content: After a short introduction into some aspects of plastic deformation (chapter 1) a systematic description of the main primary deformation processes (wire drawing, rolling, extrusion and forging) is provided (chapter 2). Chapter 3 is devoted to sheet metal forming (deep drawing, bending and folding, stretching).
H0R73A.learningOutcomes: The purpose of this course is to provide a technical and scientific description of the main plastic forming techniques and of the impact of this forming process on the properties of the end product.
H0R73A.prerequisites: An introduction course on Materials Engineering.
H0R73A.evaluation: Type: Exam during the examination period. Assessment method: Written. Type of questions: Open questions, Closed questions. Permitted materials: Course material, Calculator

H0R74A.name: Aircraft Materials
H0R74A.content: 1. Fibers: Production and properties of carbon fibers and glass fibers; Properties of polymer fibers and natural fibers 2. Matrices: Thermosets and thermoplastics; Significance and properties of the matrix 3. Micromechanics of composites: Micromechanics of unidirectional continuous fiber composites; Micromechanics of composites with short fibers 4. Mesomechanica composites: Laminate theory for layered materials; Hygrothermal tensions; Fracture criteria 5. Mechanical characterization of composites 6. Hybrid materials: Fiber-metal laminates; Sandwich materials 7. Production of composites: Impregnation and consolidation; Thermoset and thermoplastic composites 8. Use Properties of composites: Fracture toughness; Impact behaviour; Fatigue; Environmental influences
H0R74A.learningOutcomes: Understand how metal properties relate to composition and microstructure; Apply concepts to mechanical behavior of aircraft alloys; Understand composite properties using quantitative models; Acquire knowledge about constituent materials and production processes; Design laminates under simple load conditions
H0R74A.evaluation: Written exam with open questions; Metals (30%); Composite materials (70%): computer exercise using ESACOMP (30%) and other questions (40%)

H0R77A.name: Aircraft Materials and Processing Technology for Composites
H0R77A.content: The page lists three learning activities: Aircraft Materials: Part Metals (8 hours) covering dislocation movement, strengthening mechanisms, and applications to aluminum, titanium, magnesium, and steel alloys; Design and Applications of Polymers and Composites: Lecture (13 hours) addressing time dependent behavior of polymers, sandwich materials, design and optimization of joints, maintenance and repair of composites; Design and Applications of Polymers and Composites: Case Studies (13 hours) where students must (re)engineer a polymer or a composite component, in groups of 3-5 students.
H0R77A.learningOutcomes: To understand how the properties of metals are related to their composition and microstructure; To apply this knowledge on composites to solve a scientific-technological problem; To demonstrate a systematic approach to analyse a scientific-technological problem
H0R77A.evaluation: Written exam on metals (30%), project report evaluation (35%), and individual oral exam (35%)
H0R77A.lecturer: Desplentere Frederik; Swolfs Yentl; Vrancken Bey

H0R78A.name: Helicopters
H0R78A.content: The hovering helicopter, Factors affecting hover, The vertical flight, Momentum theory of forward flight, The blade element method in forward flight, Performance estimates, Performance characteristics, Rotor flapping characteristics, Trim and static stability, Main rotor design considerations, Airfoils for rotor blades, Anti-torque systems, Empennages and wings, Preliminary design, Other configurations, Helicopter noise, Helicopter vibration, Helicopter accidents
H0R78A.learningOutcomes: Includes understanding extensive subject matter in Engineering and Military Sciences; applying information to solve complex problems; communicating conclusions in writing and orally; thinking critically with evidence-based approaches; and practicing lifelong learning attitudes.
H0R78A.evaluation: Exam outside of the normal examination period, conducted as Written assessment. The professor arranges an examination moment with the students, within or outside the standard examination period.

H0T48A.name: Drive Systems
H0T48A.content: The content spans two main components. For Electrical Drives: Basic Concepts of control, measuring, mechanical couplings and power electronics for drives, including DC drives, AC drives (induction and synchronous machines), servo drives, and linear actuators with applications in transportation and robotics. For Mechatronic Drive Systems: Mechatronics and motion control systems covering actuator transduction, piezoelectric actuators, shape-memory-alloy actuators, and emerging technologies.
H0T48A.learningOutcomes: Insight in the construction, functioning and use of drives on the basis of electrical actuators, completed with power electronics, sensors and controls.
H0T48A.evaluation: This exam consists of two parts, matching both teaching activities of the course. The final mark is the average of the marks on both course components. Electrical drives component uses written open-book exam; Mechatronic drives uses open-book format with calculator permitted.

H0T49A.name: Mechatronic Drive Systems
H0T49A.content: Mechatronics and motion control systems; Aspects of dynamics and control; Actuators in mechatronics systems; Transduction: basics and constitutive equations; Sensing/actuating; Impedance matching; Figures of merit; classification; Piezoelectric actuators; Shape-memory-alloy actuators; Magnetostrictive actuators; Electro- and magnetorheological fluid actuators; Other emerging actuator technologies; Research trends and application trends
H0T49A.learningOutcomes: The student is able to analyse the elements and structure of mechatronics systems; in particular emerging actuation technologies such as piezo, magnetostrictive, shape-memory, electro-rheological, actuators. Particular attention is paid to the integration aspects, such as interaction of the actuator with the mechanical system, modelling and dimensioning.
H0T49A.evaluation: Exam during the examination period; Assessment method: Written; Type of questions: Open questions; Permitted materials: Course material, Calculator; open book, simple calculator allowed.

H0T50A.name: Tribology
H0T50A.content: General introduction, Interaction between surfaces, Tribological properties of metals and surfaces, Lubricant properties and testing them, Hydrodynamic lubrication, Hydrostatic lubrication, Elastohydrodynamic (EHD) lubrication, Sealing, Damage and degradation in tribological components, Interaction between bearings and mechanical systems, and Application in mechanical engineering
H0T50A.learningOutcomes: Provide theoretical and practical knowledge on lubrication, friction and wear in machine construction, necessary in designing, maintaining and following up bearing systems, cog wheels and ridges and various other machine components.
H0T50A.evaluation: Graded exercises throughout the semester (50%), an assignment (per 1 or 2 students) at the end of the semester (50%). Re-examination is possible in the case of failure at the first exam opportunity.

H0T52A.name: Aircraft MRO, Maintenance, Repair & Overhaul
H0T52A.content: Procedures and rules governing the Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul (MRO) of aircraft, covered from both the technical and the economic side.
H0T52A.learningOutcomes: Provide insight and knowledge into the procedures and rules of aircraft MRO, from both a technical and an economic perspective.
H0T52A.prerequisites: Basic knowledge of aircraft systems and instruments.
H0T52A.evaluation: Type: Exam during the examination period. Assessment method: Written. Type of questions: Open questions. Permitted materials: None.
H0T52A.teachingMethods: Lecture combined with a field trip.

H0T54A.name: Automotive Structures and Vehicle Dynamics
H0T54A.content: General construction and compartments; Lightweight carriage: self-carrying - space frame, aluminium - steel - synthetics; Power and energy flows in crashes; Design of energy absorbing parts (crumple zones, longitudinal sleepers); Basic elements rigid body dynamics; Longitudinal dynamics: power balance, dynamic characteristics of the drive line, vehicle performance; Transverse dynamics (drive stability); Vehicle control: influence of steering wheel and wheel suspension; Influence of tires on vehicle behaviour; Numerical simulation techniques for vehicle dynamics; Active and semi-active suspension
H0T54A.learningOutcomes: Offer knowledge on the design of vehicle bodies, with special attention to weight-saving constructions and safety aspects such as crumple zones and to acquire insight and knowledge concerning the dynamic behaviour of vehicles in particular in connection to longitudinal and transverse stability on the road.
H0T54A.prerequisites: Knowledge of machine construction, numeral techniques, mechanical vibrations, kinematics and dynamics.
H0T54A.evaluation: Open book exam and report on a case study. Study assignment in which the students do research on a technologically state of the art vehicle, in groups of two or more students.
H0T54A.teachingMethods: Processing the theory and applying a numeral simulation package on a case.

H0T56A.name: Noise Abatement in Machines, Vehicles and Aircraft
H0T56A.content: Basic concepts of technical acoustics; Principles of sound generation (air sound generation, fluid sound generation, construction noise generation); Principles of sound transmission; Basic principles of noise control: at the source, on the path of transmission, to the receiver; Subjective sound perception and sound quality; Measurement and analysis of noise - standards and regulations; Numerical modeling in the technical acoustics basics: finite elements and boundary element method; Noise control in the transport sector: Sources of interior and exterior vehicle and aircraft noise, specific control measures, standards and regulations
H0T56A.learningOutcomes: The student acquires the necessary technical and theoretical knowledge to design low-noise machinery and vehicles and to provide adequate noise reducing measures on existing machinery and vehicles. The student is able to consult with sound experts and to assess noise reducing measures on their technical quality. The student understands the principles and possibilities of numerical methods (FEM and BEM) for modeling the vibro-acoustic behavior of mechanical structures.
H0T56A.prerequisites: Students have mastered and are familiar with the dynamic behavior of (mechanical) systems and with the principles of the finite element method. The knowledge gained in the courses 'Beweging en trillingen' and 'Numerieke modellering in de mechanica' suffices.
H0T56A.evaluation: The exam consists of two parts which contribute equally to the final grade: an open book examination and the discussion of the report on the case study with numerical simulation software (Simcenter 3D).
H0T56A.teachingMethods: Lectures, lab work, in which, on the basis of a number of cases, the problem of noise control in general and of suppression of engine noise and vehicle and aircraft noise, in particular, will be further explained and illustrated.

H0T88A.name: Structural Optimization
H0T88A.content: The course combines theoretical foundations of structural design optimization with hands-on MATLAB exercises covering motivation for optimization, problem formulation, optimization algorithms, design sensitivity analysis, size/shape/topology optimization, and filtering techniques.
H0T88A.learningOutcomes: Students will appreciate the need for numerical optimization to improve the efficiency of a structural design, mathematically formulate a structural design optimization problem, understand the most useful design optimization techniques, and use these techniques for practical size, shape, and topology optimization problems.
H0T88A.prerequisites: Knowledge: the student knows the theoretical background of the finite element method. Skills: the student is able to use the finite element method to analyze structures under static loading and has MATLAB experience.
H0T88A.evaluation: The evaluation is based on an assignment to be solved in groups of 3 students using MATLAB.

H0T91A.name: Entrepreneurship in practice / service-learning
H0T91A.content: De student verwerft ervaring over diverse aspecten van (sociaal) ondernemerschap en ontwikkelt managementvaardigheden via participatie aan advies- en implementatieprojecten.
H0T91A.learningOutcomes: Upon completion, students can: apply entrepreneurship in practical situations, convert ideas into practice, develop skills including creativity and innovation, work in multidisciplinary teams, report on tasks in writing and orally, and reflect on functioning within projects and technology's role in achieving sustainability.
H0T91A.prerequisites: Om dit opleidingsonderdeel op te nemen, moeten studenten beschikken over de basisvaardigheden van een academische ingenieursopleiding: naast een wetenschappelijke basis dienen zij ook competenties te hebben in probleemoplossing, technisch ontwerp en innovatie.
H0T91A.evaluation: Permanente evaluatie zonder examen tijdens de examenperiode via written and oral reports, including interim and final reports (10-15 pages), presentation (15-20 minutes), and reflection components.
H0T91A.teachingMethods: Uitvoeren van creatieve en kwaliteitsvolle projecten voor een start-up, vzw, KMO, NGO, … Deze projecten hebben een duurtijd van één semester tot één jaar.

H0U79A.name: AI for Engineering Science
H0U79A.content: Reasoning algorithms (search, logic), Statistical modeling (probability), Machine learning (Naïve bayes, nearest neighbors, regression, clustering), Deep learning (neural networks, transformers), Language models, Image models.
H0U79A.learningOutcomes: Describe basic concepts, principles and techniques of AI and AI applications. Understand the inner working of modern AI tools and their applications, and have insight in the relations between these techniques. Select the appropriate AI solution for a given engineering problem. Implement a simple AI solution for several engineering problems. Understand the potential but also the limitations of the application of AI techniques.
H0U79A.prerequisites: Statistics (cf. Statistiek en data science H0R01A), Algebra (cf Toegepaste algebra H01A0B or Lineaire algebra H01T1A), Programming: Python (cf. Methodiek van de informatica H01B6B or Informatica H01T3C).
H0U79A.evaluation: Jupyter Notebook project (25% of final grade) and Final Exam (75% of final grade). Exam consists of multiple choice and open questions; closed book format.
H0U79A.teachingMethods: Asynchronous online learning through interactive online platform and video recordings.

H0V01A.name: Capita selecta ingenieurswetenschappen: Athens I
H0V01A.content: Afhankelijk van het opleidingsonderdeel gekozen en toegekend in de buitenlandse instelling na akkoord met de uitwisselingsverantwoordelijke. (Content depends on the course selected and assigned by the host institution.)
H0V01A.learningOutcomes: Inzicht verschaffen in een onderwerp binnen de ingenieurswetenschappen door middel van deelname aan een internationale uitwisseling (ATHENS).
H0V01A.prerequisites: De kennis en attitudes zoals aangebracht in de bachelor ingenieurswetenschappen, plus meeting prerequisite requirements specified in the ATHENS course catalogue.
H0V01A.evaluation: Permanente evaluatie zonder examen tijdens de examenperiode, evaluated as Medewerking tijdens contactmomenten with pass/fail grading. Assessment follows host institution rules, converted to PASS/FAIL by KU Leuven. No second examination opportunity.

H0V02A.name: Capita selecta ingenieurswetenschappen: Athens II
H0V02A.content: Afhankelijk van het opleidingsonderdeel gekozen en toegekend in de buitenlandse instelling na akkoord met de uitwisselingsverantwoordelijke. (Depends on the course selected and assigned at the foreign institution with exchange coordinator approval.)
H0V02A.learningOutcomes: Inzicht verschaffen in een onderwerp binnen de ingenieurswetenschappen door middel van deelname aan een internationale uitwisseling (ATHENS). (Provide insight into an engineering topic through participation in international exchange.)
H0V02A.prerequisites: De kennis en attitudes zoals aangebracht in de bachelor ingenieurswetenschappen, plus meeting prerequisite requirements of the chosen ATHENS course per the enrollment website.
H0V02A.evaluation: Permanente evaluatie zonder examen tijdens de examenperiode met Medewerking tijdens contactmomenten (continuous evaluation without exam; graded pass/fail based on the foreign institution's rules).

H0V03A.name: Capita selecta ingenieurswetenschappen: Summer Course I
H0V03A.content: Afhankelijk van het opleidingsonderdeel gekozen en toegekend na akkoord met de uitwisselingsverantwoordelijke.
H0V03A.learningOutcomes: Inzicht verschaffen in een onderwerp binnen de ingenieurswetenschappen door middel van deelname aan een op voorhand door de programmadirecteur goedgekeurde 'summer course'.
H0V03A.prerequisites: De kennis en attitudes zoals aangebracht in de bachelor ingenieurswetenschappen.
H0V03A.evaluation: Permanente evaluatie zonder examen tijdens de examenperiode via Medewerking tijdens contactmomenten. Grading is pass/fail, and results are converted by KU Leuven according to summer course standards.

H0V04A.name: Capita selecta ingenieurswetenschappen: Summer Course II
H0V04A.content: Afhankelijk van het opleidingsonderdeel gekozen en toegekend na akkoord met de uitwisselingsverantwoordelijke. (Depends on the course unit chosen and assigned with approval from the exchange coordinator.)
H0V04A.learningOutcomes: Inzicht verschaffen in een onderwerp binnen de ingenieurswetenschappen door middel van deelname aan een op voorhand door de programmadirecteur goedgekeurde 'summer course'. (Provide insight into a topic in engineering sciences through participation in a pre-approved summer course.)
H0V04A.prerequisites: De kennis en attitudes zoals aangebracht in de bachelor ingenieurswetenschappen. (Knowledge and attitudes acquired in the bachelor's program in engineering sciences.)
H0V04A.evaluation: Dit opleidingsonderdeel wordt geëvalueerd volgens de regels en gebruiken van de summer course ... PASS/FAIL. Assessment is based on Medewerking tijdens contactmomenten (participation during contact moments).

H9X30A.name: Electrical Drives
H9X30A.content: Basic Concepts of control, measuring, mechanical couplings and power electronics for drives. Classification of electric actuators and characterization of loads. DC drives: stationary and transient behavior, and construction and setting of control loops (torque, speed, position control). AC drives: Induction Machines - Scalar control: subsynchronous cascade, U/f control, field weakening; Derivation and implementation field oriented (FOC) and direct torque control (DTC); Synchronous machine types - Synchronous machines with emphasis on permanent magnet machines with sinusoidal control, Brushless DC Machine, Switched-reluctance machine, Stepper motors. Servo drives. Linear actuators. Selection of applications: electric transportation (hybrid and electric vehicles, trains), electrical energy (variable-speed wind turbines), robotics. Implementation aspects: Sensors (e.g. speed), Digital DSP system implementation, parasitic problems including thermal management, electromagnetic compatibility, power quality, noise and vibration, energetic aspects: efficiencies.
H9X30A.learningOutcomes: Insight into the construction, functioning and use of drives on the basis of electrical actuators, completed with power electronics, sensors and controls. This course is intended for system-integrated engineers who will have to use these drives in global systems.
H9X30A.prerequisites: Knowledge: Basic concepts of system theory, notions of control technology, basic knowledge of electrical machines. Preliminary conditions: system theory and control theory.
H9X30A.evaluation: Written exam, open book. The lab sessions are compulsory and are evaluated during the sessions themselves and count proportionally to the number of study points.

H9X38A.name: Micro-electromechanical Systems
H9X38A.content: Problems of MEMS: Technology trends in miniaturization, Moore's law. Examples of MEMS. Micromechanical building blocks. Scale effects. Micromanufacturing processes: Tool and beam based processes, machining by impact or material addition, moulding and replication, Etching and other lithographic processes, micro-assembly, process selection. Micro-fluidics: general overview, sealings and microfluidic actuators. Nanotechnology: general overview, CNT applications. Automotive MEMS: process control and packaging. MEMS packaging: general overview and trends in research. Watch making: historical overview of making small components.
H9X38A.learningOutcomes: The student is able to explain the major concepts, characteristics and features of MEMS technology with respect to the field of research, the possibilities and the most important fields of application.
H9X38A.prerequisites: Basic knowledge on machine elements, machine design and manufacturing technology.
H9X38A.evaluation: Type: Exam during the examination period. Assessment method: Oral. Type of questions: Open questions. Permitted materials: Computer. For the examination you have to discuss a scientific paper.
H9X38A.teachingMethods: Course illustrated with slides and hands-on examples of MEMS components, and students work in groups on micromanufacturing projects or attend lab visits.
H9X38A.lecturer: De Volder Michaël, Gorissen Benjamin, Zahedmanesh Houman

H9X53A.name: Energy Challenges
H9X53A.content: The overall energy issue (extensive coverage: Security of Supply, Climate Change issue, Affordability, Energy Efficiency, Renewable sources, Fossil sources, Nuclear Energy, ...). The energy issue for Belgium (in a European context).
H9X53A.learningOutcomes: Students should be able to grasp the context and motivations of the energy issue. The aim is for the students to be able to estimate and critically evaluate the possible 'solutions' in the energy-field.
H9X53A.prerequisites: Good basic knowledge in Thermodynamics (including Energy Conversion Machines and System), Electrical Energy Conversion, Physics.
H9X53A.evaluation: Written exam during the examination period with multiple choice, open questions, and closed questions. A calculator is permitted. A number of questions (with possible subquestions for each); to be solved written and closed book.

P0P84B.name: Organizational Psychology, part 2: Leadership
P0P84B.content: This course highlights the core concepts and processes in the domain of leadership, along with key theories and research findings. Students learn through literature and case discussions as well as skill-based exercises.
P0P84B.learningOutcomes: After completing this OPO, the student can: present and illustrate with an example the insights and theories covered in the domain of leadership, their core concepts and the empirical observations, make connections between the theoretical models and concepts, recognize theories and concepts discussed and apply them to organizational situations, critically evaluate advanced leadership questions based on the literature covered, recognize and apply fundamental leadership skills.
P0P84B.evaluation: Students are assessed based on assignments during the semester and on skills tests. Assessment includes participation during contact hours, portfolio, and skills test.
P0P84B.teachingMethods: Students learn the fundamental elements of what constitutes leadership through literature and case discussions as well as skill-based exercises.

W0AE0A.name: Lessen voor de 21ste eeuw
W0AE0A.content: Het interfacultair college biedt een staalkaart van actuele onderzoeksthema's in 13 lessen. Docenten uit verschillende disciplines brengen een relevant thema ter sprake dat hen nauw aan het hart ligt. Elk jaar komen andere thema's aan bod.
W0AE0A.learningOutcomes: Dit initiatief biedt een unieke gelegenheid over de grenzen van de vakdisciplines heen te kijken en de horizon te verbreden. Het komt tegemoet aan de idee van een universiteitsbrede algemene vorming.
W0AE0A.prerequisites: Er is geen specifieke voorkennis vereist.
W0AE0A.evaluation: Schriftelijk examen, type essayvragen. Het examen is open boek met toegang tot het cursushandboek. De studenten krijgen twee uur de tijd.
W0AE0A.lecturer: De Mesel Benjamin, Pattyn Bart (Coördinator), d'Hoine Pieter

D0R19A.name: Simulation Theory and Applications
D0R19A.content: Nine main areas: introduction to simulation concepts, fundamental building blocks, Arena software applications, basic and detailed model construction, statistical output analysis and optimization, complex modeling with steady-state analysis, entity transfer modeling, random variate generation, and variance reduction techniques.
D0R19A.learningOutcomes: Tackle complex business decision problems using simulation methodology, apply systematic approaches to model development and experimental design, interpret simulation findings for practical decisions, and critically evaluate models with quantitative rigor.
D0R19A.prerequisites: Sufficient knowledge of basic statistics and general computing skills; programming expertise is optional but beneficial.
D0R19A.evaluation: Assignments (max 40%) during the academic year plus a final on-campus exam (min 60%, multiple choice and open-ended). A second exam opportunity exists with potentially modified criteria.
D0R19A.teachingMethods: Lectures combined with practical assignments during the academic year, potentially in team settings.
D0R19A.lecturer: Wouter Verbeke (Inneke Van Nieuwenhuyse as substitute)

D0M90B.name: Optimization: Special Topics
D0M90B.content: Mathematical formulations of discrete optimization problems, exact solution methods such as branch-and-bound, branch-and-cut and Benders decomposition, with informal discussion of computational complexity.
D0M90B.learningOutcomes: Model discrete optimization problems and evaluate model quality; analyze algorithm runtime and computational complexity; comprehend algorithms underlying commercial solvers; develop exact solution methods for discrete optimization problems.
D0M90B.prerequisites: Sufficient knowledge of Linear Optimization and the basics of Operations Research.
D0M90B.evaluation: Written closed-book exam, open-ended questions, during the examination period. 100% of grade. Second exam opportunity follows the same format.

H09F7A.name: Polymer Processing
H09F7A.content: Overview of processing units for thermoplastics and thermosets; material selection and processing-properties relationships; extrusion modeling, nozzle design, and instability identification; injection molding cycle, mold filling, and common errors; shape stabilization and crystallization phenomena.
H09F7A.learningOutcomes: Provide a technical-scientific description of the several processing units and teach students how to modify different processing stages to achieve desired final material structure and properties.
H09F7A.prerequisites: Transport Phenomena part 1 (Bachelor level), Transport Phenomena part 2 (Master level), Polymers (Bachelor level).
H09F7A.evaluation: Written examination during the examination period, open-ended questions. Course materials and reference works may be consulted during the exam.
